requirements.requirement: On node1, every command run through sudo is recorded in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with a timestamp and user attribution.
requirements.summary: A valid global sudoers drop-in directs sudo policy records to the required file. Direct pre- and post-restart probes produced records containing timestamps, invoking user, target user, and complete commands. The configuration and existing audit data persisted across a verified restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the dedicated sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The configuration disables sudo syslog output, and bounded pre- and post-restart probes directly confirmed their unique markers appeared in the dedicated log but not /var/log/messages.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. Sudo command records were written to the required dedicated file with timestamp and user details, remained absent from the general log, and persisted and continued working after restart. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete and coherent: pre-restart health and boot identity, acknowledgement, changed post-restart identity, and recovered service/configuration/data state were all captured and corroborated by lifecycle observations.
limitations: Behavior was directly sampled with several root-invoked sudo commands; universal coverage for other invoking users is supported by the global Defaults configuration rather than an explicit non-root probe.
The lifecycle failed-service probe is unsupported on Alpine, though direct OpenRC/SSH and syslog process checks showed the relevant services healthy before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The configuration, audit-log creation, validation probes, and restart were causally connected to implementing or verifying the outcome and the mandatory restart protocol. One unnecessary retained artifact was found: the restart command redirected output to /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, which remained after completion. No package-health regression or new listening service was observed.
